name: Valerie Foushee
stance: Backs urgent federal guardrails and oversight for advanced AI from the Science Committee.

statements.text: Artificial Intelligence holds the incredible potential to transform many aspects of our society, however, it can pose grave risks without clear and rigorous oversight

Co-signed the Congressional AI Caucus Democrats' statement on the AI Action Plan, which said responsible innovation must go hand in hand with appropriate safety guardrails as developers build more powerful models such as artificial general intelligence, and objected to the plan's apparent targeting of state AI regulations.
Named co-chair of the House Democrats' Commission on AI alongside Reps. Ted Lieu and Josh Gottheimer.
While Americans are asking for real AI protections for consumers, Trump is bulldozing state-level safeguards through an executive order.
Republicans are blocking all legislation to prevent AI job cuts and protect civil rights in the age of AI, but we remain ready to pass AI guardrails immediately to protect our communities.
I urge Secretary Hegseth and the Department to withdraw any demands that would undermine established AI safety guardrails.
The White House’s AI policy framework falls far short of what is required to protect everyday Americans.
I’m proud to be an original cosponsor of the GUARDRAILS Act to repeal Trump’s Executive Order designed to prevent states from enacting AI policies that protect local communities.
In light of recent reports surrounding AI policy frameworks that preempt states from further regulating AI, I want to be very clear that I oppose any and all efforts to do so.

Demanded with Rep. Mike Thompson that OpenAI and Google DeepMind brief members of Congress on reports and lawsuits alleging chatbots were used in connection with violent acts, and said Congress must protect state AI laws.
As Co-Chair of the House Democratic AI Commission, I want to be clear that I do not support the draft AI bill proposed by Reps. Obernolte and Trahan in its current form.
I'm proud to be an original cosponsor the Human Authority over Autonomous Weapons Act to ensure that weapons systems always have a human decision-maker in control.
Met with members of the European Parliament to discuss AI and digital policy, saying the U.S. must work with allies on how AI is developed.
One of ten signers of the bipartisan letter urging House leadership to advance AI oversight, security and transparency legislation.
Democrats are ready to deliver AI safeguards, better healthcare, and lower grocery costs for the American people.
Cosponsor of the AI Education and Workforce Readiness Act, which requires independent evaluations and audits and adoption of the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
Responded to President Trump calling AI concerns a hoax by saying Trump undercuts Republican claims to care about regulating AI.
Claude’s access to paywalled Georgia voter data further demonstrates that AI corporations cannot be trusted to regulate themselves.
OpenAI claims they were fired because they mishandled information, but the firings came after the researchers raised concerns about new AI architecture possibly making AI harder to control.
